title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Public Works (MPW) from July 2021 to December 2022, rehabilitated and maintained 219.16 kilometres of rural roads. This initiative created employment opportunities for 12,166 persons living in rural communities, including 2,275 women and 54 persons with disabilities, creating 420,550 workdays that generated an estimated USD 3.2m in wages. Through this intervention, the Government promoted decent work, inclusivity and equal access to economic opportunities in rural areas. The Government of Timor-Leste demonstrated its commitment to the Rural Road Master Plan and Investment Strategy (RRMPIS) by updating the investment priorities for the years 2023 to 2027. The RRMPIS was endorsed and approved on 19 October 2022 by Roads for Development (R4D) Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Public Works. In supporting the recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic through targeted employment-intensive emergency public works for the rural poor and vulnerable, employment opportunities were created in road maintenance with the following results: Decent employment was created for 2,572 direct beneficiaries, including 1,023 women, and 8 persons living with disability, with a total of 34,562 workdays. 273.5 km of core rural roads to markets, other economic services/facilities and health services were improved. Income support was extended to enhance livelihoods, with USD 185,074 directly allocated to workers in rural communities as wages for their labour. The MPW in 2022, through capacity building and labour-based programme for Contractors, rehabilitated/maintained 35.62 kilometres to improve access and market linkages to agro-forestry communities. Employment was created for 708 beneficiaries, with 57,285 workdays in 2022. During 2022, 297 MPW and Municipal Public Works Offices were trained (28% women) on core functions relevant to rural road management.
The ILO, with support from the Government of Australia, continued its support for the National Directorate of Roads, Bridges and Flood Control (DRBFC) within the Ministry of Public Works (MPW). Through this work, the ILO: (1) continued providing technical assistance to Roads for Development (R4D) in implementing local resource-based approaches to rural roadworks that are community-based and that emphasize social inclusion and gender equality. (2) provided technical capacity for development of Rural Road Master Plan and Investment Strategy (RRMPIS) 2023-2027. (3) finalized a set of core technical guidelines for management of rural roads at national and municipal levels, including the R4D Operations Manual for rural roads management and 13 core technical guidelines. (4) provided training for governmental officials. In leveraging the technical capacity and support of the ILO with funding support from the Government of Australia and the European Union, the ILO`s Regular Budget Supplementary Account (RBSA) provided targeted support for employment-intensive emergency public projects. The ILO, with funding support from the European Union, continued its dedication to providing technical support for the implementation of rural roads rehabilitation and maintenance programme. This programme adopts employment-intensive investment approaches aimed at improving access to agroforestry areas, fostering market linkages, and facilitating both employment creation and economic opportunities in rural areas.
